reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents Coinbase features such as direct deposit, crypto allocation, borrowing, and card rewards as product claims rather than depicting a covert credential request or unverified payment transfer. The speaker links some benefits to membership, lending, or card spending, and an informational disclaimer qualifies the presentation as general product-related communication. the available video evidence does not establish deceptive conduct or an unsupported transaction outcome.

citations.quote: we want CoinBase to be the best place to manage and grow your money
You can set up direct deposit, allocate your paychecks across crypto of your choice and cash, growing your money exactly the way you want each time you get paid.
You can earn 3.5 % in USDC rewards, with weekly payouts for a Coinbase One membership.
you can lend your USDC on Coinbase.
You control when to lend, access your money whenever you want, and keep the rewards.

opening.argument: Judge, follow the proposed path for a paycheck. The speaker invites viewers to direct deposit into Coinbase and allocate that money to crypto or cash, then says the cash will start compounding and advertises weekly USDC rewards for members. He also invites customers to lend USDC while emphasizing their access to the money. This is more than a description of a financial app: it connects moving income onto the platform and putting funds to work with a recurring return. That promise-action link warrants treating the pitch as a scam solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls these product claims and notes that membership and lending are disclosed. But those conditions are the participation steps in the pitch, not reasons to disregard it: direct deposit routes paychecks into Coinbase, and lending puts USDC toward the advertised rewards. The absence of a covert credential request does not answer whether a return-focused appeal to move money is deceptive.

citations.quote: You can set up direct deposit, allocate your paychecks across crypto of your choice and cash, growing your money exactly the way you want each time you get paid.
you can lend your USDC on Coinbase.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited language describes available product actions and expressly ties one reward to membership; it does not promise that every paycheck or USDC deposit earns a particular return. The lending invitation likewise does not show a false payout, a diverted transfer, or deception. The accompanying description says the presentation is informational and not investment advice. A participation pathway alone does not establish a scam.

citations.quote: You can earn 3.5 % in USDC rewards, with weekly payouts for a Coinbase One membership.
This content is being provided to you for informational purposes only. Nothing discussed in this video is intended to be investment advice.

opening.argument: The return claims deserve scrutiny in combination. The speaker compares USDC rewards to the national average savings rate, says lending customers earned up to 10%, and invokes over $1 billion in staking rewards. Those figures are followed by a broad assurance of instant liquidity and a claim of wealth-building rates traditional institutions cannot match. A judge should consider the cumulative effect: attractive returns, evidence of others' participation, and ready access to funds are presented together to make crypto lending and staking feel exceptionally rewarding and easy. That combination supports a scam reading even without an explicit demand to transfer money during the video.

Meaning you can earn with confidence on your crypto knowing you can get instant liquidity at any time, whether for trading, or any other case.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to membership, lending, and an informational disclaimer. Those qualifications do not resolve the concern raised by the presentation's repeated emphasis on returns, scale, and liquidity. Nor does the lack of a demonstrated failed transaction verify the advertised outcomes for a prospective participant. The defense identifies product terms, but leaves the cumulative sales message largely unanswered.

citations.quote: And they've earned over $1 billion in staking rewards since 2023.
This is true wealth building with with rates and liquidity that traditional financial institutions simply cannot match.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument treats promotional figures as proof of deception without evidence that they are false. The speaker says lending rewards were earned by customers, describes the rate as "up to," and reports staking rewards since 2023; none is a guaranteed return to every viewer. The description also disclaims investment advice. Strong comparative marketing may merit scrutiny, but the cited material does not establish a scam.

opening.argument: Judge, assess what this presentation is trying to move viewers toward. Its description casts the talk as an account of how crypto expands financial possibilities, but the speaker walks through directing paychecks to Coinbase, earning USDC rewards with a membership, and lending USDC there. He closes by positioning Coinbase as a primary financial account. Read together, the educational framing functions as a sustained invitation to place income and assets inside an ecosystem offering returns. The ordinary-services framing should not obscure that solicitation when deciding whether the video is a scam pitch.

citations.quote: The traditional financial system limits your money and your ability to grow it. Ben Shen shares how crypto unlocks it.
We are letting you get paid directly into Coinbase while automatically investing and earning.
You can earn 3.5 % in USDC rewards, with weekly payouts for a Coinbase One membership.
And for those who want to supercharge their earnings, you can lend your USDC on Coinbase.
We're building the Primary Financial Account of the future.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the speaker describes products, but that does not make the talk merely neutral information. The specific sequence it cites takes viewers from paycheck allocation to rewards and lending, while the speaker describes lending as a way to increase earnings. An informational disclaimer cannot, by itself, settle how to read that practical invitation to participate.

citations.quote: You can set up direct deposit, allocate your paychecks across crypto of your choice and cash, growing your money exactly the way you want each time you get paid.
And for those who want to supercharge their earnings, you can lend your USDC on Coinbase.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A promotional purpose is compatible with ordinary financial-services content. The speaker identifies concrete services, including direct deposit and optional lending, and specifies that the USDC reward requires a Coinbase One membership. Recasting the presentation as a solicitation does not supply evidence that the services or returns are fictitious, or that viewers are sent through a deceptive transaction flow. The description explicitly frames the material as informational rather than investment advice.
